prompt: For a materially different sanitized system supplied by a qualified reviewer, produce and defend a capacity model, safe performance-test plan, scaling design and overload policy. Do not use the lesson fixture or model answers, and do not generate load against any unapproved target.
deliverables: System and user-journey boundary with objectives, workload classes, populations, units, windows and exclusions.
Demand history and forecast covering baseline, seasonality, event uplift, growth, uncertainty, model error and provisioning lead time.
Offered, accepted, rejected, completed, timely-correct goodput and retry accounting.
Latency distributions plus wait, service, queue age, concurrency, utilization, saturation and dependency evidence.
Safe load, stress, spike and soak design with representative data, generator calibration, staged ramps, aborts and recovery proof.
Measured performance curve identifying linear region, knee, objective loss, collapse or unexplored range.
Bottleneck argument using per-boundary evidence, alternatives, discriminating tests and external-validity limits.
Little's Law consistency check with matching boundary, units, interval, stationarity assumptions and measurement error.
Capacity requirement and sensitivity table including failure reserve, placement, quota, cost and ready-capacity semantics.
Autoscaling design covering signal, target, bounds, measurement, decision, provisioning, warm-up, stabilization and missing-signal behavior.
Overload design covering admission, bounded queues, priority, fairness, degradation, retry budgets and recovery.
Runbook with authorization, owners, go or no-go thresholds, rollback, reconciliation, evidence retention and post-event model update.
evidenceRequirements: Sanitized sources with provenance, timestamp, population, units, aggregation and known gaps.
Raw histograms or mergeable distributions where percentile aggregation matters.
Generator and target saturation measured separately.
At least three repeatable load points below the knee and controlled evidence around objective loss.
Failure-reserve test or calculation tied to an explicit failure unit.
Sensitivity analysis for at least three uncertain assumptions.
Reviewer-observed cleanup and proof that no unapproved target, data, cost or infrastructure changed.
Delayed reassessment using a second unseen workload.

rubric.observableEvidence: Defines journey, workload, population, units, windows, correctness and latency objectives.
Uses sourced baseline, seasonality, events, growth, uncertainty, lead time and model error.
Separates offered, accepted, rejected, completed, useful and retried work.
Uses valid latency distributions, counts, buckets, populations and tail limitations.
Shows authorization, realism, calibration, stages, aborts, recovery and cleanup.
Identifies safe region and limiting boundary with alternatives and falsifiers.
Applies Little's Law and queue intuition with matching units and assumptions.
Calculates ready capacity with sensitivity, failure unit, placement and quota.
Models complete control-loop delay, bounds, stabilization and failure modes.
Uses bounded admission, queues, degradation, retry budgets and explicit fairness.
Explains unit cost, marginal choice, commitments, lead time and decision authority.
States uncertainty, rollback, reconciliation, ownership and model-update evidence.
